Describe the function of music in various settings and cultural events

  • National anthem

6C961AF0DFE60131F15E68A86D17958E.description: Discuss and demonstrate appropriate listening behavior for various types of performances

6C95D4A0DFE60131F15D68A86D17958E.description: Music's Role and Function in Various Cultures

6C958F80DFE60131F15C68A86D17958E.description:

  • Play party
  • Folk dances/folk music
  • National anthem

6C947AB0DFE60131F15968A86D17958E.description:
Identify characteristics of teacher-selected genres or styles
  • Play party

6C93F330DFE60131F15768A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply the knowledge and skills to understand works of art in time and place

6C936AA0DFE60131F15568A86D17958E.description: Relate ideas learned or discussed in music to other situations in life (e.g., learn a song about imagination, and talk about how imagination can help you in many ways)

6C900180DFE60131F14968A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between ensemble groupings (solo vs. group)

6C8F2080DFE60131F14668A86D17958E.description:
Demonstrate and/or respond through movement to aural examples of music

  • expressive elements

Recognize basic forms and composition techniques
  • question/answer
  • call/response
  • AB
  • repeated patterns [ostinati]
  • verse/refrain
  • repeat sign
  • canon
  • ABA
  • introduction/interlude

Notate rhythmic patterns and dynamics presented by the teacher

  • f for forte

  • slow

Read simple rhythm patterns (using iconic or standard notation) consisting of:
  • whole note/rest
  • quarter note/rest
  • half note/rest
  • eighth-note pairs
  • dotted half note

6C8AFF70DFE60131F13868A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply the knowledge and skills to read and notate music

6C8A7CB0DFE60131F13668A86D17958E.description: Create a rhythmic and/or melodic composition using icons

6C89DDC0DFE60131F13468A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply skills to compose, arrange, and create music to communicate through the arts

6C899CC0DFE60131F13368A86D17958E.description: Improvise simple rhythmic and melodic ostinati accompaniments

6C8916E0DFE60131F13168A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply improvisation skills in music to communicate through the arts

6C88D2A0DFE60131F13068A86D17958E.description: Perform in groups matching tempo and dynamic changes, and following the cues of the conductor

6C883680DFE60131F12E68A86D17958E.description: Echo short rhythmic and melodic patterns on classroom instruments

6C878F00DFE60131F12C68A86D17958E.description: Perform a varied repertoire of music including instrumental accompaniments representing diverse cultures, genres, and styles

6C86EF00DFE60131F12A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate dynamics [p, f] and tempi [fast, slow]

6C85B010DFE60131F12768A86D17958E.description:
Perform the following rhythmic patterns using standard or iconic notation:
  • Whole note/rest
  • Quarter note/rest
  • Half note/rest
  • Eighth note pairs

6C852900DFE60131F12568A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply instrumental music skills to perform and communicate through the arts

6C84D7D0DFE60131F12468A86D17958E.description: Perform in groups using a steady beat, matching dynamics, following the cues of the conductor

6C83BA00DFE60131F12068A86D17958E.description:
Perform a varied repertoire of songs, including
  • patriotic
  • folk
  • Seasonal
  • spirituals

6C8329C0DFE60131F11E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate dynamics [p, f, crescendo, decrescendo/diminuendo] and tempi [fast, slow, ritardando]

6C824180DFE60131F11B68A86D17958E.description: Apply accurate pitch relationships while singing in a limited range [la-sol-mi, sol-mi-re-do]

6C81B780DFE60131F11968A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply singing skills to perform and communicate through the arts

6B655EB0DFE60131EF1168A86D17958E.description: Reflect historical and diverse cultural influences in dramatic activities

6B64E000DFE60131EF0F68A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply skills necessary to understand cultural diversity and heritage as they relate to theatre

6B64A0B0DFE60131EF0E68A86D17958E.description: Utilize dramatic play to complete a piece of open ended literature

6B641B00DFE60131EF0C68A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply skills necessary to understand the role of theatre in past and present cultures throughout the world

6B638ED0DFE60131EF0A68A86D17958E.description: Write a paragraph (fiction or nonfiction) and act out the characters in the story in dramatic play

6B62FDD0DFE60131EF0868A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply skills necessary to make connections between theatre and other non-arts disciplines

6B62B4E0DFE60131EF0768A86D17958E.description: Use music, creative movement and visual components in dramatic play

6B622BE0DFE60131EF0568A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply skills necessary to make connections between theatre and other arts

6B61A2C0DFE60131EF0368A86D17958E.description: Express impressions and observations related to dramatic activities and performances

6B612500DFE60131EF0168A86D17958E.description: Discuss what the students see in a dramatic presentation, including the quality of the acting and technical elements

6B60A2F0DFE60131EEFF68A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply skills to explain perceptions about and evaluations of theatre and theatrical performance

6B5FEB40DFE60131EEFD68A86D17958E.description: Identify technical theatre elements such as setting, sound, properties, lighting, costumes, and make-up

6B5F6ED0DFE60131EEFB68A86D17958E.description: Identify lead/principal, chorus, and role/supporting role

6B5E68D0DFE60131EEF768A86D17958E.description: Select and apply theatrical elements to communicate ideas through the creation of theatre

6B5DE490DFE60131EEF568A86D17958E.description: Participate in a performance for a class or invited audience

6B5CDBC0DFE60131EEF168A86D17958E.description: Use props, costumes, sound, and setting safely

6B5BC8E0DFE60131EEED68A86D17958E.description: Tell stories through group improvisation using original idea and conflict

6B5B4090DFE60131EEEB68A86D17958E.description: Develop and apply skills to communicate ideas through theatrical performances.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

752131F0DFE6013101A468A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

7520E010DFE6013101A368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., refined, respectful, polite, diplomatic, condescending).

752083F0DFE6013101A268A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonym/antonym, analogy) to better understand each of the words.

752032F0DFE6013101A168A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., literary, biblical, and mythological allusions) in context.

751FE380DFE6013101A068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

751F9060DFE60131019F68A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

751F1B80DFE60131019E68A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

751EB970DFE60131019D68A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., belligerent, bellicose, rebel).

751E6EC0DFE60131019C68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

751E2300DFE60131019B68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 7 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

751D86A0DFE60131019968A86D17958E.description: Choose language that expresses ideas precisely and concisely, recognizing and eliminating wordiness and redundancy.

751D3560DFE60131019868A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

751C3690DFE60131019568A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives (e.g., It was a fascinating, enjoyable movie but not He wore an old[,] green shirt).

751BE930DFE60131019468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

751B9AD0DFE60131019368A86D17958E.description: Place phrases and clauses within a sentence, recognizing and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers.

751B4590DFE60131019268A86D17958E.description: Choose among simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.

751AD8A0DFE60131019168A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of phrases and clauses in general and their function in specific sentences.

751A8410DFE60131019068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

75195860DFE60131018D68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

7518A880DFE60131018B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

75185AD0DFE60131018A68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

7517BD50DFE60131018868A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

75171330DFE60131018668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7516C430DFE60131018568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

751624B0DFE60131018368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

7515CD80DFE60131018268A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

75157310DFE60131018168A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize salient points.

75151630DFE60131018068A86D17958E.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with pertinent descriptions, facts, details, and examples; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

75145D20DFE60131017E68A86D17958E.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

75140440DFE60131017D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how the ideas clarify a topic, text, or issue under study.

75139F70DFE60131017C68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others and, when warranted, modify their own views.

75134420DFE60131017B68A86D17958E.description: Pose questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant observations and ideas that bring the discussion back on topic as needed.

7512F600DFE60131017A68A86D17958E.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

7512A610DFE60131017968A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

75124C20DFE60131017868A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 7 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

751161E0DFE60131017568A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

75111180DFE60131017468A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

7510BFA0DFE60131017368A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

751003B0DFE60131017168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

750FA6B0DFE60131017068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

750F4EF0DFE60131016F68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

750EA3C0DFE60131016D68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

750E53A0DFE60131016C68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

750DAE10DFE60131016A68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

750D5E70DFE60131016968A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

750D0950DFE60131016868A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

750CAE80DFE60131016768A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

750C5D20DFE60131016668A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

750BF940DFE60131016568A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

750B9DE0DFE60131016468A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

750ADB30DFE60131016268A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

750A7FE0DFE60131016168A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.

750A2640DFE60131016068A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

7509D860DFE60131015F68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

75098A20DFE60131015E68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

75093950DFE60131015D68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

7508D9E0DFE60131015C68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.

75087230DFE60131015B68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

7507F600DFE60131015A68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7507A760DFE60131015968A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

75075000DFE60131015868A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

7506F240DFE60131015768A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

7506A4B0DFE60131015668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

75060030DFE60131015468A86D17958E.description: Writing Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects 6—12

7505AC00DFE60131015368A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7504F650DFE60131015168A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g. "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims").

75049F30DFE60131015068A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history").

75044B20DFE60131014F68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7503F9F0DFE60131014E68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

75039540DFE60131014D68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.

750339A0DFE60131014C68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7502DF70DFE60131014B68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and link to and cite sources as well as to interact and collaborate with others, including linking to and citing sources.

75027000DFE60131014A68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

7501F9F0DFE60131014968A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

750159E0DFE60131014768A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

75010C70DFE60131014668A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

75DE8060DFE60131033F68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

75DE25F0DFE60131033E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

75DC9410DFE60131033A68A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

75DC4200DFE60131033968A86D17958E.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

75DBE180DFE60131033868A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

75DAECC0DFE60131033568A86D17958E.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian's Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

75DA9D40DFE60131033468A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

75D2F3C0DFE60131031E68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

75D2A010DFE60131031D68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

75D24880DFE60131031C68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

75D12DC0DFE60131031968A86D17958E.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

75D0E360DFE60131031868A86D17958E.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

75CE1C50DFE60131030F68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

75CD74D0DFE60131030D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

F437F689432B4BC489D367E22DAC462F.description: Analyze evidence of the factors that have caused the change in global temperatures over the past century.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of factors include human activities (such as fossil fuel combustion, cement production, and agricultural activity) and natural processes (such as changes in incoming solar radiation or volcanic activity). Examples of evidence can include tables, graphs, and maps of global and regional temperatures, atmospheric levels of gases such as carbon dioxide and methane, and the rates of human activities.]

67873179136148E5AFEEBBD351C2E5A0.description: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of the design process include examining human environmental impacts, assessing the kinds of solutions that are feasible, and designing and evaluating solutions that could reduce that impact. Examples of human impacts can include water usage (such as the withdrawal of water from streams and aquifers or the construction of dams and levees), land usage (such as urban development, agriculture, or the removal of wetlands), and pollution (such as of the air, water, or land).

30433CB3FD02433C861A8EBFC076CC0B.description: Analyze data to define the relationship for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth's systems.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of data include grade-appropriate databases on human populations and the rates of consumption of food and natural resources (such as freshwater, mineral, and energy). Examples of impacts can include changes to the appearance, composition, and structure of Earth's systems as well as the rates at which they change.

A9E5390EEAE040C58F9E00A7CB58DE8E.description: Analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effects.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how some natural hazards, such as volcanic eruptions and severe weather, are preceded by phenomena that allow for reliable predictions, but others, such as earthquakes, occur suddenly and with no notice, and thus are not yet predictable. Examples of natural hazards can be taken from interior processes (such as earthquakes and volcanic eruptions), surface processes (such as mass wasting and tsunamis), or severe weather events (such as hurricanes, tornadoes, and floods). Examples of data can include the locations, magnitudes, and frequencies of the natural hazards. Examples of technologies can be global (such as satellite systems to monitor hurricanes or forest fires) or local (such as building basements in tornado-prone regions or reservoirs to mitigate droughts).

096AD610108D4CD2813242BEBAB051A2.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth's mineral, energy, and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes and human activity.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how these resources are limited and typically non-renewable, and how their distributions are significantly changing as a result of removal by humans. Examples of uneven distributions of resources as a result of past processes include but are not limited to petroleum (locations of the burial of organic marine sediments and subsequent geologic traps), metal ores (locations of past volcanic and hydrothermal activity associated with subduction zones), and soil (locations of active weathering and/or deposition of rock).

58D7120F78C64C86ACC8A9986C0A5BEA.description: Develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and rotation of the Earth cause patterns of atmospheric and oceanic circulation that determine regional climates.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how patterns vary by latitude, altitude, and geographic land distribution. Emphasis of atmospheric circulation is on the sunlight-driven latitudinal banding, the Coriolis effect, and resulting prevailing winds; emphasis of ocean circulation is on the transfer of heat by the global ocean convection cycle, which is constrained by the Coriolis effect and the outlines of continents. Examples of models can be diagrams, maps and globes, or digital representations.

8DD0551157AA400E81ED17A3B3D7B8CA.description: Research, collect, and analyze data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses results in changes in weather conditions.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how air masses flow from regions of high pressure to low pressure, causing weather (defined by temperature, pressure, humidity, precipitation, and wind) at a fixed location to change over time, and how sudden changes in weather can result when different air masses collide. Emphasis is on how weather can be predicted within possible ranges. Examples of data can be provided to students (such as weather maps, diagrams, and visualizations) or obtained through laboratory experiments (such as with condensation).

E939E620577B4B1F8BFB0E6767149CBC.description: Design and develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth's systems driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the ways water changes its state as it moves through the multiple pathways of the hydrologic cycle. Examples of models can be conceptual or physical.

7F06019F86B943119D28F577396E5A29.description: The Role of Water in Earth's Surface Processes

922C88F3BB7C4B3B943BC4648891E090.description: Analyze and interpret data on the distribution of fossils and rocks, continental shapes, and seafloor structures to provide evidence of the past plate motions.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of data include similarities of rock and fossil types on different continents, the shapes of the continents (including continental shelves), and the locations of ocean structures (such as ridges, fracture zones, and trenches).

75BAB5D47D9A4891A2E92B82B0D76899.description: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth's surface at varying time and spatial scales.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how processes change Earth's surface at time and spatial scales that can be large (such as slow plate motions or the uplift of large mountain ranges) or small (such as rapid landslides or microscopic geochemical reactions), and how many geoscience processes (such as earthquakes, volcanoes, and meteor impacts) usually behave gradually but are punctuated by catastrophic events. Examples of geoscience processes include surface weathering and deposition by the movements of water, ice, and wind. Emphasis is on geoscience processes that shape local geographic features, where appropriate.

4EEDFE617B6B413DB778845B4076DC24.description: Develop and use a model to illustrate that energy from the Earth's interior drives convection which cycles Earth's crust leading to melting, crystallization, weathering and deformation of large rock formations, including generation of ocean sea floor at ridges, submergence of ocean sea floor at trenches, mountain building and active volcanic chains.
comments: Clarification Statement: The emphasis is on large-scale cycling resulting from plate tectonics that includes changes in rock types through erosion, heat and pressure.

4B67E0D58E8F43689AE57E7F932FD826.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence from rock strata for how the geologic time scale is used to organize Earth's history.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how analyses of rock formations and the fossils they contain are used to establish relative ages of major events in Earth's history. Examples of Earth's major events could range from being very recent (such as the last Ice Age or the earliest fossils of homo sapiens) to very old (such as the formation of Earth or the earliest evidence of life). Examples can include the formation of mountain chains and ocean basins, the evolution or extinction of particular living organisms, or significant volcanic eruptions.

BA2BE5B13C934E52A89292B378820932.description: Analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of scale properties include the sizes of an object's layers (such as crust and atmosphere), surface features (such as volcanoes), and orbital radius. Examples of data include statistical information, drawings and photographs, and models.

04886A1BAE4244EB8816950DFEA142A2.description: Develop and use a model to describe the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis for the model is on gravity as the force that holds together the solar system and Milky Way galaxy and controls orbital motions within them. Examples of models can be physical or conceptual.

0CBA9D9CC8D846CFA5A5DE9DD122DFA0.description: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun system to explain the cyclical pattern of seasons, which includes the Earth's tilt and directional angle of sunlight on different areas of Earth across the year.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of models can be physical, graphical, or conceptual.

81BFF3277FF64B9E9194436D31ED8B9B.description: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to explain the cyclic patterns of lunar phases and eclipses of the sun and moon.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of models can be physical, graphical, or conceptual and should emphasize relative positions and distances.

88F63B92364340B29C2060AE52FE350E.description: Interpret graphical representations to support explanations of how natural selection may lead to increases and decreases of specific traits in populations over time.

8CD70BECC2E3435A9CCF2489EC7EDCF9.description: Gather and synthesize information about the technologies that have changed the way humans influence the inheritance of desired traits in organisms.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on synthesizing information from reliable sources about the influence of humans on genetic outcomes in artificial selection (such as genetic modification, animal husbandry, and farming practices).

050BC619E24C41E28AE1DB279C3EF4F0.description: Construct an explanation based on evidence that describes how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some individuals' probability of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on using simple probability statements and proportional reasoning to construct explanations.

3998BA95AC83415AB9858FF49CD6F031.description: Analyze and interpret evidence from the fossil record to infer patterns of environmental change resulting in extinction and changes to life forms throughout the history of the Earth.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence include sets of fossils that indicate an environment, anatomical structures that indicate the function of an organism in the environment, and fossilized tracks that indicate behavior of organisms.]

9236A41CF8C74A058DD46CF1763AD662.description: Evidence of Common Ancestry and Diversity

7AC8F3367E0343EDB913B7D361AE223E.description: Evaluate benefits and limitations of differing design solutions for maintaining an ecosystem.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of design solutions could include water, land, and species protection, and the prevention of soil erosion. Examples of design solution constraints could include scientific, economic, and social considerations.

661F4AB04FE5425385559A1DAAA16A68.description: Construct an argument supported by empirical evidence that explains how changes to physical or biological components of an ecosystem affect populations.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on recognizing patterns in data and making inferences about changes in populations, defining the boundaries of the system, and on evaluating empirical evidence supporting arguments about changes to ecosystems.

849D46333A67463BBD8B9A374E53B44D.description: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on describing the conservation of matter and flow of energy into and out of various ecosystems, including food chains and food webs.]

49F87282E9DA4C74A9167957835D9480.description: Cycles of matter and Energy Transfer in Ecosystems

61170F3D54584B6285D484E492951759.description: Construct an explanation that predicts the patterns of interactions among and between the biotic and abiotic factors in a given ecosystem.
comments: Clarification Statement: Relationships may include competition, predation, and symbiosis.

BF8A9A329E4E4F90842639889DDA9D57.description: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for the effects of resource availability on individual organisms and populations of organisms in an ecosystem.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on cause and effect relationships between resources and growth of individual organisms and the numbers of organisms in ecosystems during periods of abundant and scarce resources.

C608590EEA6844E7B463328100F5215B.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.

566EC15F3A38456C809F3C4137335F20.description: Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in Organisms

EA3DEF8812EA4B5DB03606CA76021BB5.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors influence the growth of organisms.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of local environmental conditions could include availability of food, light, space, and water. Examples of genetic factors could include large breed cattle and species of grass affecting growth of organisms. Examples of evidence could include drought decreasing plant growth, fertilizer increasing plant growth, different varieties of plant seeds growing at different rates in different conditions, and fish growing larger in large ponds than they do in small ponds.]

D290DBD59F444265B0C89D804A7E1A16.description: Construct an explanation for how characteristic animal behaviors as well as specialized plant structures affect the probability of successful reproduction of animals and plants respectively.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of animal behaviors that affect the probability of animal reproduction could include nest building to protect young from cold, herding of animals to protect young from predators, and vocalization of animals and colorful plumage to attract mates for breeding. Examples of animal behaviors that affect the probability of plant reproduction could include transferring pollen or seeds; and, creating conditions for seed germination and growth. Examples of plant structures that affect the probability of plant reproduction could include bright flowers attracting butterflies that transfer pollen, flower nectar and odors that attract insects that transfer pollen, and hard shells on nuts that squirrels bury.]

9243F9F4C11644F299032FC6818723F7.description: Present evidence that body systems interact to carry out key body functions, including providing nutrients and oxygen to cells, removing carbon dioxide and waste from cells and the body, controlling body motion/activity and coordination, and protecting the body.

EADAA382CE57426E991A7802AC042722.description: Develop an argument supported by evidence for how multicellular organisms are organized by varying levels of complexity; cells, tissue, organs, organ systems.

9D7616AF6D6F4765BCE245C7E5353602.description: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways parts of the cells contribute to that function.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the cell functioning as a whole system and the primary role of identified parts of the cell, specifically the nucleus, chloroplasts, mitochondria, cell membrane, and cell wall.

C4A791E15F644A7B9A3E70CF976AC523.description: Provide evidence that organisms (unicellular and multicellular) are made of cells and that a single cell must carry out all of the basic functions of life.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on developing evidence that living things are made of cells, distinguishing between living and non-living things, and understanding that living things may be made of one cell or many and varied cells.

4D9274F4C8404508AAD90DA3E072D780.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structure and Processes

FECA91E8735A4CAB9599BF8019BFF435.description: Develop and use a model to describe that waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on both light and mechanical waves. Examples of models could include drawings, simulations, and written descriptions.

C0E0561CBC0A4E9E9D190435CFC966D5.description: Use mathematical representations to describe a simple model for waves that includes how the amplitude of a wave is related to the energy in a wave.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on describing waves with both qualitative and quantitative thinking.

2C2E280FA4384C8A84FB967CF41C0753.description: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

AD5457431EF948A0A84735F7CCD35A0C.description: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of empirical evidence used in arguments could include an inventory or other representation of the energy before and after the transfer in the form of temperature changes or motion of object.

E5F8AC7E747B469E989EE35AB8EB6A7E.description: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer

B257082FB20D4AA9B5578F65EC68D20D.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine the relationships among the energy transferred, the type of matter, the mass, and the change in the temperature of the sample.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of experiments could include comparing final water temperatures after different masses of ice melted in the same volume of water with the same initial temperature, the temperature change of samples of different materials with the same mass as they cool or heat in the environment, or the same material with different masses when a specific amount of energy is added.

1D3E64CB4E264464AC8F7935BDE7F9C0.description: Apply scientific principles to design, construct, and test a device that either minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of devices could include an insulated box, a solar cooker, and a Styrofoam cup.

BBF130C456A04EB8A6E6BB8D5C81A5A7.description: Develop a model to describe that when the arrangement of objects interacting at a distance changes, different amounts of potential energy are stored in the system.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on relative amounts of potential energy, not on calculations of potential energy. Examples of objects within systems interacting at varying distances could include: the Earth and either a roller coaster cart at varying positions on a hill or objects at varying heights on shelves, changing the direction/orientation of a magnet, and a balloon with static electrical charge being brought closer to a classmate's hair. Examples of models could include representations, diagrams, pictures, and written descriptions of systems.]

65A411D74E0B487F8CA248454A4874F2.description: Construct and interpret graphical displays of data to describe the relationships of kinetic energy to the mass of an object and to the speed of an object.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on descriptive relationships between kinetic energy and mass separately from kinetic energy and speed. Examples could include riding a bicycle at different speeds, rolling different sizes of rocks downhill, and getting hit by a whiffle ball versus a tennis ball.]

26A43E05546A49D4A897F674AB2257E2.description: Conduct an investigation and evaluate the experimental design to provide evidence that electric and magnetic fields exist between objects exerting forces on each other even though the objects are not in contact.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of this phenomenon could include the interactions of magnets, electrically-charged strips of tape, and electrically-charged pith balls. Examples of investigations could include first-hand experiences or simulations.

BE3B5185FB314C7D9A8049FE31627EFD.description: Create and analyze a graph to use as evidence to support the claim that gravitational interactions depend on the mass of interacting objects.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evidence for arguments could include data generated from simulations or digital tools; and charts displaying mass, strength of interaction, distance from the Sun, and orbital periods of objects within the solar system.

883FCDC918F7437EB78EE14F3A501714.description: Analyze diagrams and collect data to determine the factors that affect the strength of electric and magnetic forces.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of devices that use electric and magnetic forces could include electromagnets, electric motors, or generators. Examples of data could include the effect of the number of turns of wire on the strength of an electromagnet, or the effect of increasing the number or strength of magnets on the speed of an electric motor.

942FBDE763704DF294B43C1F59D99516.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object's motion depends on the sum of the forces on the object and the mass of the object.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on balanced (Newton's First Law) and unbalanced forces in a system, qualitative comparisons of forces, mass and changes in motion (Newton's Second Law), frame of reference, and specification of units.

7CC2DA294510440C8DB810AF410B4B01.description: Apply physics principles to design a solution that minimizes the force of an object during a collision and develop an evaluation of the solution.

6AF0EEDE66F347E7B0035871C6C6DE00.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

577CE424D17443A4ADC8FBF5993A6305.description: Construct, test, and modify a device that either releases or absorbs thermal energy by chemical processes.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the design, controlling the transfer of energy to the environment, and modification of a device using factors such as type and concentration of a substance. Examples of designs could involve chemical reactions such as dissolving ammonium chloride or calcium chloride.

EBA5D364D29C4855B0AB1BC518E40443.description: Develop and use a model to describe how the total number of atoms remains the same during a chemical reaction and thus mass is conserved.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on law of conservation of matter and on physical models or drawings, including digital forms that represent atoms.

1E6D4487793C49D09E15BC76258233E8.description: Develop a model that describes changes in particle motion, temperature, and state of a pure substance when thermal energy is added or removed.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on qualitative molecular-level models of solids, liquids, and gases to show that adding or removing thermal energy increases or decreases kinetic energy of the particles until a change of state occurs. Examples of models could include drawings and diagrams. Examples of particles could include molecules or inert atoms. Examples of pure substances could include water, carbon dioxide, and helium.

A8A18ADB7D074A8892CE1C1F5601FBF9.description: Gather, analyze, and present information to describe that synthetic materials come from natural resources and how they impact society.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on natural resources that undergo a chemical process to form the synthetic material. Examples of new materials could include new medicine, foods, and alternative fuels.

E9DF41E564EB4280BE902CCF012AACE1.description: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of reactions could include burning sugar or steel wool, fat reacting with sodium hydroxide, and mixing zinc with hydrogen chloride.]

DF4B88F4929543028E713472E26D00D9.description: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on developing models of molecules that vary in complexity. Examples of simple molecules could include ammonia and methanol. Examples of extended structures could include sodium chloride or diamonds. Examples of molecular-level models could include drawings, 3D ball and stick structures, or computer representations showing different molecules with different types of atoms.

document.title: Missouri Learning Standards: English Language Arts (6-12)

218FB0F74BFF49BB850AE89F7662A0C8.description: Plan and deliver appropriate presentations based on the task, audience and purpose including multimedia components in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize significant points.

9C7272A4ABFE4A18939B873C9A833523.description: Position body to face the audience when speaking and makes eye contact with listeners at various intervals using effective gestures to communicate a clear viewpoint.

DDC980BDED9F43848B971BF648AB4267.description: Speak clearly, audibly, and to the point, using conventions of language as appropriate to task, purpose and audience when presenting including volume at an understandable pace.

F06E2067756842E0809A0FF2085E1DD1.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others including those presented in diverse media and, when warranted, modify their own views.

5F96939A34E64226A06C300B78AC6EBE.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and claims, evaluating reasoning in order to pose questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant observations and ideas that bring the discussion back on topic as needed.

92948517E0FA49DFA6DC36340A2EDEC8.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions and decision-making, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

A3CDF2F21A9A484992CF2EC26B01F198.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, writing and link to and cite sources as well as to interact and collaborate with others, including linking to and citing sources.

44CE1D3C594F4BFA8FA0E10EF3D66FC1.description: Use effective transitions to clarify relationships and connect ideas, claims and signal time shifts.

E6D4E71969C34EEDB8A1A48444AD9758.description: Conventions of standard English and usage: Demonstrate a command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage, including spelling and punctuation.

361C44D2CA4A411383C17D5DA90ADED2.description: Word choice, syntax, and style: Choose appropriate precise language for the style, task and audience; convey the relationship among ideas through varied sentence structures.

244F6D09CC1B434B8ED6A5764365C5BE.description: Organization and Content: Introduce the topic, maintain a clear focus throughout the text, and provide a conclusion that follows from the text. Add or delete content to clarify meaning.

3590DBA0E66C4EA7844B144250960165.description: Review, revise, and edit writing with consideration for the task, purpose, and audience.

155024A9437240C3AD3F1322FD3748B4.description: Approaching the Task as a Reader

1B7F651542AA4A28A50C67DC5CA1D1A9.description: Argumentative: Develop argumentative writing by introducing and supporting a claim with clear reasons and relevant evidence; acknowledging counterclaims; establishing relationships between claims and supporting evidence.

959AFEE50BA343519A45FEBB7FE80491.description: Expository: Develop informative/explanatory writing to examine a topic with relevant facts, examples, and details; establish relationships between ideas and supporting evidence.

53FF3A8F491F4FAE96F8F30051536D31.description: Narrative: Develop narratives including poems about real or imagined experiences, which establish and maintain a consistent point of view, and include clearly identified characters, well-structured event sequences, narrative techniques and relevant, descriptive details.

B9D2574450CD4B4EBC1F6B05AEC915B5.description: Follow a writing process to produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, style, and voice are appropriate to the task, purpose and audience; develop writing with narrative, expository, and argumentative techniques.

BD9CD8F249414BDD9806EE33AA736881.description: Approaching the Task as a Writer

AECD9104336C493AA9214F6A1DB6CE64.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

2C9EB2F1775B4111B6911D478D59BC55.description: Conduct research to answer a question; gather relevant sources, print and digital; integrate information using a standard citation system.

D2B99B36A1144802A76D795FDD4E9929.description: Approaching the Task as a Researcher

8D09298A16A04CBCBF0738A79D5D51B6.description: Read and comprehend informational text independently and proficiently.

0C75C5D0F0FE495481FC311AE9918DB8.description: Explain how the text reflects historical and/or cultural contexts.

1BDF082977B94C9F95106121DFDFA2A4.description: Compare and contrast how two or more authors writing about the same topic make decisions about craft and structure.

E3E8B4B343BD4D23A8AAC575FE99EF68.description: Compare and contrast information presented in different mediums and analyze how the techniques unique to each medium contribute to meaning.

AC8381AA37F641EEA290EDE45E39BF65.description: Synthesize Ideas from Multiple Texts (Approaching Texts as a Researcher)

3500E1368DC74284ABCB51F10D429EA5.description: Evaluate an author's argument, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

931F3F06D8C44EE189CF924A679A3D13.description: Analyze how word choice contributes to meaning and tone.

93F14706038E4D329E34818D8B99C230.description: Analyze how an author develops his/her point of view or purpose and distinguishes it from those of others.

643217A3A0D14C49B0CF9ACF76CAB8BC.description: Analyze how a text's organization or overall structure contributes to meaning.

E00FC7D189F248ABA68B28DCC23E5C3B.description: Analyze Craft and Structure (Approaching Texts as a Writer)

2E394A6E17C84A738CDBF8514E451D92.description: Explain the central/main idea(s) of a text and explain the relationship between the central idea(s) and supporting evidence; summarize the text distinct from personal opinions.

DB2EBF1499114DF4AC7BC83B875C6BA7.description: Interpret visual elements of a text including those from different media and draw conclusions from them (when applicable).

F6494495B5804481AFDA1C2B4B8E6850.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative, connotative, and content-specific meanings using context, affixes, or reference materials.

E2E1A9750CE04BDA98E8B0A7F774875C.description: Draw conclusions, infer and analyze by citing several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

C81B52A8EBCA4F418D39BF6989226936.description: Comprehend and Interpret Texts (Approaching Texts as a Reader)

10269A496D47437EB5A6E6F2F69D6300.description: Read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas and poems, independently and proficiently.

282D315C7D08415FB15930F90495AFEA.description: Explain how characters and settings reflect historical and/or cultural contexts.

DBCDF1FE17F04F6DA004CDBA09C981A6.description: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character with realistic accounts of the same subject matter.

6394B716F4CF4CBCA6486E97DB137D56.description: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version, analyzing how the techniques unique to each medium contribute to meaning.

E9948CF10D224654AB340B32433CA6AF.description: Synthesize Ideas from Multiple Texts (Approaching Texts as a Researcher)

8AA0C467795A4A1599E570DF2AB6D3F4.description: Analyze how the setting, characters, and plot of a text affect each other and contribute to meaning.

57213BECA34B45FD8C67B4FF6A4CFD7E.description: Analyze how specific word choices contribute to meaning and tone.

9581AD1DA43C42F791607FDB5AB305E3.description: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.

ACDEE92E79374405A5A30E01B4A973CF.description: Analyze how a text's form or overall structure contributes to meaning.

27D3475ABF8F48C6A02782F6F481872A.description: Using appropriate text, determine the theme(s) of a text and explain the relationship between the theme(s) and supporting evidence; summarize the text distinct from personal opinions.

49A810666248477CB72D5756053115F2.description: Interpret visual elements of a text and draw conclusions from them (when applicable).

E0712263AF0347F2BB5CA5C0CF093FD5.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings using context, affixes, or reference materials.

07F3F9EB8D384B498A6178D4FDB670CF.description: Draw conclusions, infer and analyze by citing several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

55EE30F41D7F4D2AA7BA12EFB3B7B7C2.description: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

88C971D0858548DBAE52372C9639DECE.description: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.

6BB188C34D484509B77491D000B791C5.description: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through the development of a new or improved object or tool.

BD5197B2B4F34BFAA8163D9457C328D7.description: Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the land, water, air, and/or other living things in the local environment.

A2FB90A55DE948B58AE917426694ECC0.description: Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants or animals (including humans) and the places they live.

BCDC28EF6E1C493986D180806C7D6409.description: With prompting and support, construct an argument using evidence for how plants and animals (including but not limited to humans) can change the environment to meet their needs.

659C67DDA59C4D48BBED674D6225F6AE.description: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of qualitative observations could include descriptions of the weather (such as sunny, cloudy, rainy, and warm); examples of quantitative observations could include numbers of sunny, windy, and rainy days in a month. Examples of patterns could include that it is usually cooler in the morning than in the afternoon and the number of sunny days versus cloudy days in different months.

54738F2A57B54C07A01AA3C3312419FF.description: Make observations during different seasons to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on relative comparisons of the amount of daylight in the winter to the amount in the spring or fall.

1F1F4715E5234AD48A324B09853B831F.description: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of patterns could include that animals need to take in food but plants do not; the different kinds of food needed by different types of animals; the requirement of plants to have light; and, that all living things need water.

43FF7F4D53F2400CBE55C61CE8CB450C.description: Organization for Matter and Energy Flow in Organisms

E4FE25E2F693455A8A524D661461A27E.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structure and Processes

0A517BB9A13042C7B92E0A182528F7E8.description: With prompting and support, use tools and materials to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area

68610C264946492980407D2D530D997B.description: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer

CD65185703C84783A0948604387F16F5.description: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth's surface.

6FFF692F1A1E4979B5869E7F968A1A64.description: Describe ways to change the motion of an object (i.e., how to cause an object to go slower, go faster, go farther, change direction, stop).

78C05829ADA14DF9B35B9E01470E80C6.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to compare the effects of different strengths or different directions of pushes and pulls on the motion of an object.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of pushes or pulls could include a string attached to an object being pulled, a person pushing an object, a person stopping a rolling ball, and two objects colliding and pushing on each other.]

B8015696399443C29B1A261DDD7F8545.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

163E18CCF7054428898F3BF70C146648.description: Make qualitative observations of the physical properties of objects (i.e., size, shape, color, mass).

CD5458F5031742AD89F161B47D2BF52A.description: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

2EA68E5DCA7041C8BA6028E713F14E2A.description: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.

7AD6DE90FCDE40E587AEC943D622FE84.description: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through the development of a new or improved object or tool.

7544EEEE300E4BAA8D3406428FBEDA33.description: Identify patterns indicating relationships between bserved weather data and weather phenomena (e.g., temperature and types of precipitation, clouds and amounts of precipitation).

8377F406B0F14495850F937BBDA2C167.description: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of patterns could include that the sun and moon appear to rise in one part of the sky, move across the sky, and set; and stars other than our sun are visible at night but not during the day.

67BE5377BB764B619843BAD9F114BA22.description: Describe the presence of the Sun, Moon, and stars in the sky over time.

5B646DDF416440B988BD7D1911348F17.description: Make observations to construct an evidence based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of patterns could include features plants or animals share. Examples of observations could include leaves from the same kind of plant are the same shape but can differ in size; and, a particular breed of dog looks like its parents but is not exactly the same.

5543263F1425487A8A2E7685E3B7EB1D.description: Understanding Connections: Demonstrate understanding of relationships between music and the other arts, other disciplines, varied contexts, and daily life.

1785A5EC42444DD98B10C70C2B6B5C28.description: Relate artistic ideas and works with societal, cultural, and historical context to deepen understanding

199548389CB04E969735059B5F7DB5E4.description: Making Connections: Demonstrate how interests, knowledge, and skills relate to personal choices and intent when creating, performing, and responding to music.

CF3E946C56464571AA8D1AA706C8A9F6.description: Synthesize and relate knowledge and personal experiences to make art

BAF861CE26AB4156A7218DA80EA1F80E.description: Evaluate: Explain the influence of experiences, analysis, and context on interest in and evaluation of music.

F1374C912E3F40C6B8BC9E51C7600996.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work

A2B7157E3FD24265BFA2BCC81B9EF1A5.description: Interpret: Identify and support interpretations of the expressive intent and meaning of musical works, citing as evidence the treatment of the elements of music, contexts, and (when appropriate) the setting of the text.

32CC2A8DFC6D46CEA7E6AFE79E522F36.description: Interpret intent and meaning in artistic work

A8A4E793E28D49ABBE255ECABF3BF971.description: Analyze: Describe how understanding context and the way the elements of music are manipulated inform the response to music.

B12C8DC541F1422D9E9E3BFAADB53E00.description: Select: Explain reasons for selecting music citing characteristics found in the music and connections to interest, purpose, and context.

8DA5C9695E5C4D039A38EFA78CADCEF4.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work

56F17E61DCC443C997BE5E0847CD46B5.description: Evaluate the validity and reliability of claims in published materials of the effects that different frequencies of electromagnetic radiation have when absorbed by matter.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that photons associated with different frequencies of light have different energies, and the damage to living tissue from electromagnetic radiation depends on the energy of the radiation. Examples of published materials could include trade books, magazines, web resources, videos, and other passages that may reflect bias.

A939232293AB495F969240DABFC2E32E.description: Communicate technical information about how electromagnetic radiation interacts with matter.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples could include solar cells capturing light and converting it to electricity; medical imaging; and communications technology.

5A0EE9BE82374096A659E6304AD290E5.description: Evaluate the claims, evidence, and reasoning behind the idea that electromagnetic radiation can be described either by a wave model or a particle model, and that for some situations one model is more useful than the other.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on how the experimental evidence supports the claim and how a theory is generally modified in light of new evidence. Examples of a phenomenon could include resonance, interference, diffraction, and photoelectric effect.

F65D1340B6194A83901A208215591B80.description: Use mathematical representations to support a claim regarding relationships among the frequency, wavelength, and speed of waves traveling in various media.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of data could include electromagnetic radiation traveling in a vacuum and glass, sound waves traveling through air and water, and seismic waves traveling through the Earth.

6DD4DFC159EC4FE08ED4FCDF8A2ACF1A.description: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

F79A61333A284BA787EF1DFDCD11B371.description: Develop and use a model of two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields to illustrate the forces between objects and the changes in energy of the objects due to the interaction.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of models could include drawings, diagrams, and texts, such as drawings of what happens when two charges of opposite polarity are near each other.

A8DA7594F41E4B999E92A699835B48DC.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the transfer of thermal energy when two components of different temperature are combined within a closed system results in a more uniform energy distribution among the components in the system (second law of thermodynamics).
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on analyzing data from student investigations and using mathematical thinking to describe the energy changes both quantitatively and conceptually. Examples of investigations could include mixing liquids at different initial temperatures or adding objects at different temperatures to water.

F5034468EA0A4D649608C0ED2CE88EE8.description: Conservation of Energy and Energy Transfer

49666D2539B545C996E0AD48B58241EC.description: Design, build, and refine a device that works within given constraints to convert one form of energy into another form of energy.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on both qualitative and quantitative evaluations of devices. Examples of devices could include Rube Goldberg devices, wind turbines, solar cells, solar ovens, and generators. Examples of constraints could include use of renewable energy forms and efficiency.

E78009C2B0394445AD9E76B7E0CC1AE8.description: Develop and use models to illustrate that energy at the macroscopic scale can be accounted for as a combination of energy associated with the motions of particles (objects) and energy associated with the relative position of particles (objects).
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of phenomena at the macroscopic scale could include the conversion of kinetic energy to thermal energy, the energy stored due to position of an object above the earth, and the energy stored between two electrically-charged plates. Examples of models could include diagrams, drawings, descriptions, and computer simulations.

8805DC213A584BD0A329C53610DAB65D.description: Create a computational model to calculate the change in the energy of one component in a system when the changes in energy are known.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on explaining the meaning of mathematical expressions used in the model.

22EC0298825C46D5B68FD491BBB8BA7E.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that an electric current can produce a magnetic field and that a changing magnetic field can produce an electric current.

DEF671F8FB874060B742AE8BBBD84E3A.description: Use mathematical representations of Newton's Law of Gravitation to describe and predict the gravitational forces between objects.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on both quantitative and conceptual descriptions of gravitational fields.

C35E9679E7D8412DBB1DA8BBB4260E8D.description: Apply scientific principles of motion and momentum to design, evaluate, and refine a device that minimizes the force on a macroscopic object during a collision.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of evaluation and refinement could include determining the success of the device at protecting an object from damage and modifying the design to improve it. Examples of a device could include a football helmet or a parachute.

A66F39BDC2E04E65AB20FFBBB6E40BDA.description: Use mathematical representations to support and verify the concepts that the total momentum of a system of objects is conserved when there is no net force on the system.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the quantitative conservation of momentum in interactions and the qualitative meaning of this principle.

9974339F2F33474BB9167B2B173C06F1.description: Analyze data to support and verify the concepts expressed by Newton's 2nd law of motion, as it describes the mathematical relationship among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of data could include tables or graphs of position or velocity as a function of time for objects subject to a net unbalanced force, such as a falling object, an object rolling down a ramp, or a moving object being pulled by a constant force.

DBD132A90BBF44268E0465FB0724B1DD.description: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

11B572B33C9A4742927F5A29D75C4753.description: Use symbolic representations to illustrate the changes in the composition of the nucleus of the atom and the energy released during the processes of fission, fusion, and radioactive decay.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on simple qualitative models, such as pictures or diagrams, and on the scale of energy released in nuclear processes relative to other kinds of transformations.

063E4DC4E841415A8C0FFBB6419E8588.description: Use symbolic representations and mathematical calculations to support the claim that atoms, and therefore mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on conservation of matter and mass through balanced chemical equations, use of the mole concept and proportional relationships.

1669C5D3288942A8BF81BDC776947A8D.description: Refine the design of a chemical system by specifying a change in conditions that would alter the amount of products at equilibrium.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the application of Le Chatelier's Principle and on refining designs of chemical reaction systems, including descriptions of the connection between changes made at the macroscopic level and what happens at the molecular level. Examples of designs could include different ways to increase product formation including adding reactants or removing products.

9A9543A55CA54293BFAC99BC55AD3A6C.description: Apply scientific principles and evidence to provide an explanation about the effects of changing the temperature or concentration of the reacting particles on the rate at which a reaction occurs.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on student reasoning that focuses on the number and energy of collisions between molecules.

93C22ECBAD1A4E829ABD2AF61C6B49EE.description: Develop a model to illustrate that the release or absorption of energy from a chemical reaction system depends upon the changes in total bond energy.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the idea that a chemical reaction is a system that affects the energy change. Examples of models could include molecular-level drawings and diagrams of reactions, graphs showing the relative energies of reactants and products, and representations showing energy is conserved.

DABFD606DD1240C1BC394AF8C2C02717.description: Apply the concepts of bonding and crystalline/molecular structure to explain the macroscopic properties of various categories of structural materials, i.e. metals, ionic (ceramics), and polymers.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on the attractive and repulsive forces that determine the functioning of the material. Examples could include why electrically conductive materials are often made of metal, flexible but durable materials are made up of long chained molecules, and pharmaceuticals are designed to interact with specific receptors.

AE9E1471DE1A4228AAAB73019BCB8753.description: Plan and conduct an investigation to gather evidence to compare physical and chemical properties of substances such as melting point, boiling point, vapor pressure, surface tension, and chemical reactivity to infer the relative strength of attractive forces between particles.
comments: Clarification Statement: Emphasis is on understanding the relative strengths of forces between particles. Examples of particles could include ions, atoms, molecules, and networked materials (such as graphite).

2B1DF07FE17940208014B8CCBC763B97.description: Construct and revise an explanation for the products of a simple chemical reaction based on the outermost electron states of atoms, trends in the periodic table, and knowledge of the patterns of chemical properties.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of chemical reactions could include the reaction of sodium and chlorine, or of oxygen and hydrogen.

D00D1F56121C4527BFB3762FE81E7996.description: Use the organization of the periodic table to predict the relative properties of elements based on the patterns of electrons in the outermost energy level of atoms.
comments: Clarification Statement: Examples of properties that could be predicted from patterns could include reactivity of metals, types of bonds formed, numbers of bonds formed, and reactions with oxygen.
